title: A finite purely inseparable extension descends along a field extension
statement: Let $K\subseteq L$ be fields ($L$ a field extension of $K$ [def-pc-field-extension]) and let $B$ be a commutative $K$-algebra. Regard $L\otimes_KB$ as an $L$-algebra via $l\mapsto l\otimes1$. If $L\otimes_KB$ is a field and, via this map, a finite purely inseparable field extension of $L$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], then $B$ is a field, the structure map $K\to B$ makes $B$ a finite purely inseparable field extension of $K$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension], and $\dim_KB=\dim_L(L\otimes_KB)$.

source.place: Implicit in the proof of Lemma Tag 07QG (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-subfields, line 47202), where $k_i'$ is asserted to be a finite purely inseparable field extension of $k_i$ without argument; definition of purely inseparable: Fields, Definition Tag 09HE (fields.tex). Intended argument (agent): choose a $K$-basis of $L$ containing $1$ and a $K$-basis $(b_\lambda)$ of $B$ containing $1$; then $(1\otimes b_\lambda)$ is an $L$-basis of $L\otimes_KB$, so $\dim_KB=\dim_L(L\otimes_KB)<\infty$, and $b\mapsto1\otimes b$ is injective; hence $B$ is a domain finite over $K$, so a field; if $\beta\in B$ has $(1\otimes\beta)^q=l\otimes1$ ($q$ a power of the characteristic exponent), comparing coordinates in the basis $(1\otimes b_\lambda)$ gives $\beta^q\in K$; in characteristic $0$, $\dim=1$ gives $B=K$.

proof.text: *Step 2 (a basis of $B$ containing $1$).* Since $1\neq0$ in $B$ (step 1), by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-basis-through-vector] the $K$-vector space $B$ has a $K$-basis $(b_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ with an index $0\in\Lambda$ such that $b_0=1$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QG (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-subfields, line 47202): the assertion that $k_i'$ is finite purely inseparable over $k_i$, made without argument; argument written by an agent

proof.text: *Step 3 (the basis of $A$; finiteness and dimension).* By [def-weil-vector-space-scalar-extension], $(b_\lambda\otimes1)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is an $L$-basis of the extension of scalars $B\otimes_KL$; the swap $B\otimes_KL\to L\otimes_KB$, $b\otimes l\mapsto l\otimes b$, is an $L$-linear isomorphism (both sides being the base change of [def-weil-module-base-change], with $L$ acting on the $L$-factor), so $(1\otimes b_\lambda)_{\lambda\in\Lambda}$ is an $L$-basis of $A$. By hypothesis $A$ is finite-dimensional over $L$, say $\dim_LA=d$; a basis of a $d$-dimensional space has exactly $d$ elements [def-weil-vector-space-dimension], so $\Lambda$ is finite with $|\Lambda|=d$. Hence $(b_\lambda)$ is a finite $K$-basis of $B$: $B$ is finite-dimensional over $K$ [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace] and $\dim_KB=|\Lambda|=d=\dim_L(L\otimes_KB)$, the last assertion of the statement.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QG (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-subfields, line 47202): the assertion that $k_i'$ is finite purely inseparable over $k_i$, made without argument; argument written by an agent

proof.text: *Step 4 ($B$ is a domain).* The map $\iota:B\to A$, $b\mapsto1\otimes b$, is a ring homomorphism ($1\otimes1$ is the unit and $(1\otimes b)(1\otimes b')=1\otimes bb'$) and is injective: if $b=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda b_\lambda$ ($c_\lambda\in K$, finitely many nonzero) then $\iota(b)=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda(1\otimes b_\lambda)$ with coefficients the images of $c_\lambda$ in $L$, which vanish only if all $c_\lambda=0$, because $(1\otimes b_\lambda)$ is $L$-linearly independent (step 3) and $K\to L$ is injective. So $B$ is isomorphic to a subring of the field $A$; with $1\neq0$ in $B$ (step 1) it follows that $B$ is an integral domain.

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QG (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-subfields, line 47202): the assertion that $k_i'$ is finite purely inseparable over $k_i$, made without argument; argument written by an agent

proof.text: *Step 5 ($B$ is a finite field extension of $K$).* By steps 3 and 4, $B$ is a commutative $K$-algebra that is an integral domain and finite-dimensional over $K$, so $B$ is a field by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field]. With its structure map $K\to B$ it is a field extension of $K$ [def-pc-field-extension], finite because $\dim_KB=d<\infty$ (step 3), as required by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

source.place: Lemma Tag 07QG (lemma-geometrically-regular-over-subfields, line 47202): the assertion that $k_i'$ is finite purely inseparable over $k_i$, made without argument; argument written by an agent

proof.text: *Step 6 (purely inseparable, characteristic $p>0$).* Suppose $\operatorname{char}K=\operatorname{char}L=p>0$ and let $\beta\in B$. By hypothesis and [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] applied to $A/L$, the element $1\otimes\beta$ satisfies $(1\otimes\beta)^{p^n}\in L$ for some $n\ge0$, i.e. $(1\otimes\beta)^{p^n}=l\otimes1$ for some $l\in L$. Since $\iota$ is a ring homomorphism (step 4), $(1\otimes\beta)^{p^n}=1\otimes\beta^{p^n}$. Write $\beta^{p^n}=\sum_\lambda c_\lambda b_\lambda$ with $c_\lambda\in K$. Then in $A$, $\sum_\lambda c_\lambda(1\otimes b_\lambda)=1\otimes\beta^{p^n}=l\otimes1=l\cdot(1\otimes b_0)$ (as $b_0=1$). Comparing coefficients in the $L$-basis $(1\otimes b_\lambda)$ (step 3) gives $c_\lambda=0$ for $\lambda\neq0$ (and $c_0=l$). Hence $\beta^{p^n}=c_0b_0=c_0\cdot1\in K$. So every element of $B$ is purely inseparable over $K$, and $B/K$ is purely inseparable [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension].

source.place: Definition Tag 09HE (purely inseparable); argument written by an agent

proof.text: *Step 7 (purely inseparable, characteristic $0$).* Suppose $\operatorname{char}K=\operatorname{char}L=0$. Then by [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension] the hypothesis says $A=L$, i.e. $L\to A$, $l\mapsto l\otimes1$, is bijective, so $d=\dim_LA=1$. By step 3, $|\Lambda|=1$, so $\Lambda=\{0\}$ and $B=K\cdot b_0=K\cdot1$: the structure map $K\to B$ is surjective, and it is injective since $K$ is a field and $B\neq0$. So $B=K$, which is the definition of purely inseparable in characteristic $0$ [def-weil-pbc-finite-purely-inseparable-extension]. Together with steps 3, 5 and 6 this proves the statement.
